idea: Themed weeks, week five, Money day: written from the source, then corrected by a numbers editor and a viewer editor before voicing.
description: At end-March 2025 Gujarat had 13.0 scheduled commercial bank offices per lakh projected population (1 lakh = 100,000), against 8.7 in Jharkhand: 49% more (India: 11.9). In the 2023-24 survey (NFHS-6), 91% of women aged 15-49 in Jharkhand had a bank account they use themselves, against 82% in Gujarat (India: 89%).

In the earlier survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) the order was the same: Jharkhand 80%, Gujarat 70%, India 79%. Jharkhand was more than 5 points ahead of Gujarat in both surveys. Gujarat's offices per lakh people were 1.48 to 1.50 times Jharkhand's in each year from 2020 to 2025. These are rates: in total, at end-March 2025, Gujarat had 9,513 offices and Jharkhand 3,518. Across the states and UTs, offices per person and women's own accounts were weakly linked in 2023-24. Offices are those of scheduled commercial banks; population is projected (National Commission on Population, July 2020 edition), and seven north-eastern states share one projection. The women's figures are survey estimates. The map leaves out Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. The table shows how much, not why.
source: Reserve Bank of India, Handbook of Statistics on Indian States 2024-25 (Dec 2025), Table 152: offices of scheduled commercial banks, end-March 2025, over projected population (National Commission on Population, July 2020 edition, 1 March 2025). Women's own account: IIPS, NFHS-6 (2023-24) and NFHS-5 (2019-21) state fact sheets, women aged 15-49, survey estimates. Seven north-eastern states share one population projection.
question: Which matters more: offices or accounts?

done: Writer built the pair from RBI Table 152 offices over projected population and the NFHS-6 and NFHS-5 women's own-account figures, and recomputed them with python3 (Gujarat 1.48 to 1.50 times Jharkhand's offices per lakh in every year 2020 to 2025; rank correlation 0.20 across states in 2023-24). Numbers editor recomputed from the data files and fixed a hook and title that read 'more women with accounts' as a head count (now rates, with 'per person' in the title), the state count on the weak-link card (dropped, because Delhi matches on both sides), the chip period and the source line (publisher named, survey estimates). Viewer editor replaced a hook that copied px09's 'A more X, B more Y' shape with a question hook, moved '49% more' to card 1, explained 'lakh', put 2019-21 in place of 'NFHS-5' on card 3 and dropped 'only' from 'only weakly linked'.
